summary: This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make any alien convicted of harming animals used in law enforcement inadmissible to the United States and deportable.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends immigration law to add grounds of inadmissibility and deportability for a specific criminal conviction. It contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
The legislation does not mention firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill directly amends sections 212 and 237 of the Immigration and Nationality Act to render any alien convicted of harming law-enforcement animals inadmissible or deportable. This adds a new enforcement mechanism that restricts immigration by expanding the grounds for removal and denial of entry.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not address military or defense budgets or policy.
No environmental or regulatory provisions are present.
The bill contains no welfare, benefits, or entitlement provisions.
No education-related content appears in the bill.
The legislation does not address controlled substances or drug enforcement.

While the bill references an existing federal criminal statute (18 U.S.C. 1368) as a trigger for immigration consequences, it does not alter criminal sentencing, policing practices, or rehabilitation programs; any effect on criminal justice is incidental and secondary to its immigration purpose.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are included.
The bill has no fiscal or debt-related implications.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill does not mention foreign assistance or aid programs.
No election, voting access, or election-integrity measures are present.
The legislation contains no technology, data, or privacy regulations.
No labor, employment, or union-related provisions appear.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
